Class CodeBlock

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.processing.source.CodeBlock
public final class CodeBlock extends Object
A fragment of code: statements, an expression, or Javadoc text, with placeholders for the types and names it refers to. 
CodeBlock block = CodeBlock.newBuilder()
        .addStatement("$T<$T> names = new $T<>()", List.class, String.class, ArrayList.class)
        .beginControlFlow("for ($T user : users)", User.class)
        .addStatement("names.add(user.name())")
        .endControlFlow()
        .build();

The placeholders are $T for a type (TypeName, Class, Type, TypeMirror or TypeElement), imported as needed; $N for a name (a String, or a Parameter, Field, Method or Type); $S for a string literal, escaped, or null; $L for anything written as is, such as a number, another code block, an annotation or an anonymous class; $$ for a dollar sign; $> and $< to indent and unindent the lines that follow; $[ and $] to start and end a statement, whose lines after the first are indented twice more; $W for a space, and $Z for nothing, where the line breaks if what follows would go past column 100. Arguments are taken in order, or by position with $1T, $2N and so on, but not both in one format; or by name with $type:T, from a map given to CodeBlock.Builder.addNamed(String, Map).

A format and its arguments do not match when a placeholder is not one of these, has no argument, or has an argument it cannot write, such as a $T argument that is not a type or is a local or anonymous class, which has no name; when an argument is not used; or when a format takes its arguments both in order and by position.

A code block may be a fragment that indents or starts a statement for another one to close. One that stands on its own, such as the body of a method, the initializer of a field or Javadoc, must be balanced: it must not unindent or end a statement more than it indents or starts one, and must close all it opens.

Code blocks are values: two blocks with the same text and arguments are equal.

      public static Collector<CodeBlock, ?, CodeBlock> joining(String separator, String prefix, String suffix)
      Returns a collector that joins code blocks with a separator, between a prefix and a suffix, such as "(" and ")". The prefix and the suffix are written even when there is no block.
      Parameters:
      separator - the text between two blocks, written as is
      prefix - the text before the first block, written as is
      suffix - the text after the last block, written as is
      Returns:
      the collector
